landscape.label: Local Know-How
landscape.title: Window Tinting in Seattle After the 2021 Heat Dome
landscape.sub: Downtown Seattle · South Lake Union · Belltown
landscape.say: The late June 2021 heat wave changed how a lot of Seattle homeowners think about their windows. The city logged three straight days over 100 degrees, and many houses had no air conditioning because for most of the twentieth century they simply did not need it. Upstairs bedrooms in older homes stayed hot well after midnight, and portable units struggled to keep up.

landscape.label: Why Window Film Here
landscape.title: Why Seattle Window Film Has to Handle Two Different Suns
landscape.say: Seattle sits far enough north that the sun behaves very differently from one season to the next. Around the June solstice, daylight runs about sixteen hours, the sun climbs high, and a west window can take direct light well past 8 p.m. In December the days shrink to roughly eight and a half hours, and even at noon the sun stays under twenty degrees above the horizon.

Office: Office window film for downtown and South Lake Union floors where curtain walls create monitor glare, hot perimeter desks and cold interior zones. Storefront: Storefront film for Seattle retail and restaurants that blocks UV fading on displays, softens afternoon glare for diners and can add a layer of break-in resistance. Commercial Security: Commercial security film for glass doors and display windows that slows smash-and-grab entry and holds shattered glass in place.

landscape.label: How It Works
landscape.title: How an install works

tiles.s: Fill out the quote form with your address
They look at glass type, frame condition
The crew protects floors and sills
Film needs time for the mounting solution to dry out

landscape.say: Here's how an install works. First, fill out the quote form with your address, which rooms or floors bother you, and what the problem is: heat, glare, fading, privacy or security. Then, they look at glass type, frame condition and which way each window faces, then hold film samples up so you can compare them in your own light. On install day, the crew protects floors and sills, cleans each pane thoroughly, then applies film cut to the edge of the glass. Finally, film needs time for the mounting solution to dry out.
